slides.headline: They just realised who is sitting at their table.
The stranger
slides.text: Two followers of Jesus meet a stranger on the road to Emmaus. At supper he blesses the bread, and everything changes.

slides.headline: The face
slides.text: This is Jesus, but young and beardless. Caravaggio broke the rules, so that we, like them, don't recognise him at first.

slides.headline: The chair
slides.text: On the left, one follower grips his chair, about to jump up. His elbow seems to push right out of the painting.

slides.headline: Open arms
slides.text: On the right, the other throws his arms wide in shock. His hand almost reaches out of the canvas toward us.

slides.headline: The innkeeper
slides.text: Only the innkeeper, standing with his cap on, understands nothing. To him, this is just another hungry guest at his table.

slides.headline: The basket
slides.text: Now look at the fruit basket, balanced on the very edge of the table. One more second and it falls to the floor.

slides.headline: Wrong season
slides.text: And look at the fruit itself: grapes and figs, more like autumn than spring, when the story is set. A clue, or a slip?

slides.headline: Would you?
slides.text: A stranger walks beside you all day, and only at dinner you realise who he is. Would you believe your own eyes?
